threads.thread_goal: Align on sitemap, navigation, and page priorities for the redesign.

messages.text: Hi team, here is the first draft of the sitemap and page inventory for the redesign. You can find it in A2. This covers the work for T2. Let me know what you think. @24711 @530681
Thanks! Taking a look now.

Thanks @277618. I'm reviewing A2 and it seems a few key sections are missing compared to the current site, like 'Careers' and 'Investor Relations'. Could you please double-check against the audit report A1 from T1 to ensure we have full coverage before we finalize the structure?
Oh, you're right. I missed those. Sorry about that, I'll review A1 and update the sitemap.
Good catch. Also, what are our thoughts on the 'Blog'? Should it be a top-level navigation item or nested under a 'Resources' section?
I've updated A2 with the missing pages. For the blog, I've put it under 'Resources' for now, but we can change it.

Thanks for the quick update. The structure in A2 looks complete now. Nesting 'Blog' under 'Resources' is a good starting point; it helps streamline the primary navigation. I'm happy to approve this sitemap structure.

Now for the scope of the first release. To align with marketing's goals for lead conversion, I propose we prioritize the following pages: Homepage, About Us, all Product pages, Pricing, and the Contact Us flow. This gives us a complete user journey to launch with.
That scope makes sense. It's focused on the core business objectives. I agree with that list.
Sounds good. I will mark those pages in A2 as 'Phase 1'.
Perfect. We have our decisions. D1: Sitemap structure is approved. D2: First release scope is confirmed. I'll log this in our decision tracker. @277618, please ensure A2 is fully updated by EOD.

threads.thread_goal: Select the visual direction and core UI components.

messages.text: Team, for T3, I've prepared two moodboards to guide our visual direction. Please take a look and share your feedback. Link is in Figma.

Here are screenshots for quick reference.
Option A: 'Modern & Minimal' - clean, spacious, with a focus on typography.
Option B: 'Bold & Vibrant' - energetic, with strong colors and more expressive visuals.
These look fantastic! I'm immediately drawn to Option B. It feels more confident and aligns with the forward-looking brand image we want to project.
I like both of them. Option A seems like it might be simpler to build and make responsive.

@277618 That's a fair point. Both directions are technically feasible, but Option B will require more rigorous application of our grid and type scales on mobile to maintain clarity. It's a challenge I'm confident we can handle.
Given the positive feedback on Option B, I've started drafting some core UI components based on that style for T5. You can see the initial set for buttons, forms, and cards in the draft of A3.
The components in A3 look great. The primary CTA button has a lot of impact. This will definitely help with conversion.
I've shared this with the brand manager as well, and they are strongly in favor of Option B. With this alignment, I propose we officially select the 'Bold & Vibrant' direction.
Ok, I'm good with Option B.
Let's do it. Option B is the winner.

Great. Decision D3 is confirmed. Now, let's finalize the initial component set in A3. I've listed: Buttons, Form Inputs, Cards, and Navigation elements. Does this cover what we need for the priority pages?
We should probably add a Banner/Alert component. We often have announcements on the homepage.
Excellent point. I'll add Banners to the list in A3. With that addition, we can lock this initial set.
Decisions D3 and D4 are locked and have been logged in A7. @277618, you can now begin applying this direction to the wireframes for the layout templates in T4.

threads.thread_goal: Review and iterate on key page layouts and prototypes.

messages.text: Hi team, I've finished the first pass on the high-fidelity mockups for the homepage and product pages (T6). I've also created a basic interactive prototype in A4 for the main user journey (T7). Please take a look. @24711 @530681
On it! Excited to see them.

Thanks @277618. This is a solid first version. I've left some detailed comments in Figma, but here are the highlights:
1. Homepage Layout (T4): The mobile hero section feels crowded. The main headline is wrapping to four lines. Let's explore a smaller font size for that breakpoint or adjust the wording.
2. Prototype (A4): The flow from the product page to the 'Request a Demo' form is a bit jarring. It feels like a hard redirect.
Ok, I see the issue with the mobile headline. I can try to reduce the font size. For the prototype, what kind of change were you thinking of?
I agree on the prototype flow. Maybe we could use a modal window for the form instead of a separate page? It would keep the user in context.
A modal sounds like a good idea. I haven't built one in this prototype tool before, so I'll have to figure that out.

A modal is the right approach, @530681. @277618, I can send you a link to a similar component from another project for reference. Please work on that and the mobile homepage fix. Let's aim to have the revisions ready for review tomorrow.
Ok, will do. Thanks for the help.
Hi team, I've updated the mockups and the prototype in A4 with the requested changes. The modal is now in place and the mobile homepage layout should be better.

Just reviewed the updates. This is a huge improvement. The mobile layout has room to breathe, and the modal flow is much more seamless. I've logged the changes in our feedback doc A7. With these revisions, I'm ready to approve the layouts.
Are there any other final UX changes we need to make before we freeze these designs and prepare for handoff?
None from me. I think this is in a great place.
Excellent. Then we have our decisions. D5: Key page layouts are approved. D6: No further UX changes, designs are frozen. Let's move on to final documentation.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize content, imagery, and SEO-related design requirements.

messages.text: Hi everyone, I've created a draft of the Web Content and Imagery Style Guide (A6) as part of T10. It covers tone of voice, hero image specs, and illustration style. Would love your feedback. @24711 @277618
Thanks, I'll take a look.

Thanks @530681, this is a comprehensive start. The imagery guidelines are very clear. One critical addition we need is a section on SEO best practices for content, which is part of T11. We should specify rules for H1/H2 usage, meta descriptions, and image alt-text to ensure the marketing team has clear direction.
That's a great point, I was focused on the visual and brand voice aspects. I'll add a dedicated SEO section and sync with the marketing lead to make sure it covers their needs. Thanks!
Quick question - where are we getting the images from? Do we have a stock photo account?
Yes, our preferred stock vendors are listed in section 3 of the guide A6. We have subscriptions with them.
Update: I've added the SEO guidelines to A6 and had marketing review them. Their feedback is incorporated. I believe the document is now ready for final approval.
Just reviewed the new version. The SEO section is perfect and provides the clarity we need. This document is solid. I approve the web content and imagery style guide.
Excellent! Decision D7 is confirmed. I'll circulate the final version of A6 to the broader content and marketing teams so they can start using it.

threads.thread_goal: Confirm handover readiness and rollout plan for redesigned pages.

messages.text: Hi, I'm working on the design handover package for T9. I've filled out the readiness checklist in A5. I think it's mostly ready for the dev team. @24711

Thanks @277618. I'm looking at the checklist A5 and see a couple of key items from the T9 definition of done are not yet checked: 'Specs for spacing, typography, and states documented' and 'Exported assets provided in required formats'. Can you clarify the status of these?
Oh, I thought the specs were clear enough in the Figma file itself. I can add more detailed annotations. I will export all the assets this afternoon.
Please do. We need explicit annotations for spacing, states, etc., to prevent any guesswork from the dev team. Let's ensure A5 is 100% complete before we schedule the official walkthrough.

While the handover package is being finalized, I've drafted the Redesign Rollout Plan (A8) for T12. It outlines a phased launch, starting with the homepage and product pages. Please review and let me know your thoughts.
The phased approach in A8 is the right way to go, it minimizes risk. I've left a couple of comments regarding content dependencies for Phase 2. Once those are addressed, the plan looks solid.
Update: I've added all the detailed annotations and exported the assets. The handover checklist A5 is now fully complete.
And I've updated the rollout plan A8 with your feedback, @24711.

Fantastic work, team. I've done a final check of the handover package and the rollout plan. Everything is in order. I'm signing off that the designs are ready for development and the rollout plan is approved.
Decision D8 is confirmed. @277618, please schedule the dev walkthrough for T9 for tomorrow morning. @530681, please share the final A8 with all project stakeholders.
